audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion in both layers; the mirror (nautilus__sion) is already set to Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion, Sion, Sion, Sion and the packet agrees with the mirror.
audit.why: Level 2 is not a Sion stage — Dredge Line is online and you have no dash to answer a hook. Levels 4-5 and 6 are his worst stages: armour shred plus shield volume beat his rotation and he has no escape from a charged Q.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3 and 4 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group to match the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named Dredge Line repeatedly but never gave its cooldown or range, so 'track it' had nothing concrete behind it.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — the longest cooldown in his lane kit and the whole reason his whiff is a free window. Riptide is only 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, so a whiffed hook still leaves him a slow.
audit.corrected: whys[1], spikes[3] and mid now carry 14s / 1150 range and name Riptide as what is left after the whiff.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told the player that Sion has no dash out of a landed hook, or what Flash is actually for in this lane.
audit.why: Dredge Line pulls you together and Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you; with no mobility in Sion's kit the escape is Flash, and it must be saved for the hook rather than spent on damage. Dredge Line into terrain also pulls him, so he can re-close after a retreat.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] and wants.foe[0] now state it.

edits.before: His Dredge Line is off cooldown so respect the hook angle, but your W-shield already negates his auto damage; probe with a short Q to set him up for level 3.
edits.after: Dredge Line is up (14s at rank 1) so respect the 1150-range hook angle, but Soul Furnace already eats his auto damage; probe with a short Q to set up level 3.

edits.before: Dredge Line is his only real threat: one hooked Sion gives him a full passive-root auto chain into his team's response, his only real window to swing the lane.
edits.after: Dredge Line is his only real threat: hooked, you have no dash out, so his Staggering Blow root chain lands free — hold Flash for the hook, not the damage.

edits.before: From level 3 onward you run the lane. Every trade cycle is Q-telegraph into E-shred into W-shield burst — Nautilus has no answer to your armor shred or your shield volume. The only check on your pattern is Dredge Line: track its cooldown, and the instant you see it hit the ground wide or come off cooldown on a wave where he is inside charged-Q range, commit immediately. At level 6 your Unstoppable Onslaught makes every Dredge Line whiff an automatic kill attempt — R in, land the full charged Q, and his HP pool has no way to survive the armor-shredded brawl.
edits.after: From level 3 onward you run the lane. Every trade cycle is Q-telegraph into E-shred into W-shield burst — Roar of the Slayer's armour shred plus your shield volume beat his rotation. The only check is Dredge Line (14s at rank 1, 1150 range): once it whiffs into terrain he has nothing left but Riptide's slow, so commit the moment he is inside charged-Q range. At level 6 Unstoppable Onslaught makes every Dredge Line whiff a kill attempt — R in, land the full charged Q, and his HP pool cannot survive the armour-shredded brawl once Titan's Wrath expires.

edits.before: Your late game against Nautilus is a free side-lane stomp: he cannot 1v1 a two-item Sion whose W-shield alone absorbs his entire trading rotation, and your zombie passive means he risks losing a fight even after killing you. Play the wave to force him into a 1v1 or let your team engage while you absorb Dredge Line as a frontline target. The only thing that can go wrong is a roam-heavy Nautilus buying time for his carries — track his R and treat his missing-from-lane timer as an urgent call to either match the roam with your own R transit or take the tower immediately.
edits.after: Your late game against Nautilus is a free side-lane stomp: he cannot 1v1 a two-item Sion whose W-shield alone absorbs his entire trading rotation, and your zombie passive means he risks losing a fight even after killing you. Play the wave to force him into a 1v1 or let your team engage while you absorb Dredge Line as a frontline target. The only thing that can go wrong is a roam-heavy Nautilus buying time for his carries — track Depth Charge (120s at rank 1) and treat his missing-from-lane timer as a call to match the roam with your own R transit or take the tower.

edits.before: Land Dredge Line to trigger his passive root and chain autos before you can retaliate
